name: compute_cross_product_components
description: Computes the cross product of two three-component vectors held in a structure and writes the three result components back into it. It calls an unnamed routine during the computation.

name: return_constant_two
description: Returns the fixed value 2 with no other work. It is a small stub that a pointer in data refers to.

name: return_constant_three
description: Returns the fixed value 3 with no other work. It is a small stub that a pointer in data refers to.

name: return_constant_four
description: Returns the fixed value 4 with no other work. It is a small stub that a pointer in data refers to.

name: return_constant_five
description: Returns the fixed value 5 with no other work. It is a small stub that a pointer in data refers to.

name: classify_value_into_band
description: Compares a 16-bit input against a descending set of fixed thresholds and returns a band number together with the boundary value for that band. It is called from six places.

name: update_object_motion_damped
description: Advances the first position component of an object by scaled velocity terms, clamps it, and then, for each axis whose magnitude exceeds fourteen, applies a shift-based damping to its vector components and decrements a per-axis countdown byte, restarting it at sixty when it underflows.

name: damp_second_and_third_axes
description: Applies the same clamped motion, shift-based damping and countdown update to the second and third position components of the object, continuing the pass started by the first-axis routine.

name: apply_axis_velocity_and_damp
description: Adds an input velocity to the first position component of an object, clamps it against a limit, and applies shift-based damping to its vector components and countdown byte. It then runs the same clamped damping pass for the second and third components.

name: damp_object_axes_limited
description: Runs the clamped shift-based damping pass over the second and third position components, adjusting each vector and decrementing its countdown byte. Helper routines supply the shift count and the timer reset value.

name: damp_axis_group_by_sign
description: Chooses the damping direction from the sign of a field in the object, then applies shift-based damping and countdown updates to a group of components before returning.

name: apply_input_velocity_and_damp
description: Adds an input velocity to the second position component, clamps it against the limit, damps that component group, and then runs the clamped damping pass for the third component.

name: damp_axis_group_mirrored
description: Selects the damping direction from the sign of a field in the object, then applies shift-based damping and countdown updates to a group of its components. It then returns.

name: stub_return_immediately
description: Contains only a return and performs no work.

name: apply_input_velocity_damp_third
description: Adds an input velocity to the third position component, clamps it against the limit, and applies shift-based damping to that axis group's vector components and countdown byte.

name: stub_return_no_operation
description: Contains only a return and performs no work.

name: shift_and_store_offsets
description: Shifts two 16-bit fields of the object right by three and two bits, negates the second result, and stores both values in other fields of the same object.

name: compute_dot_product_clamped
description: Computes two dot products of the object's basis vectors with a reference vector and stores them in fields of the object, zeroing a third value. When the third dot product is negative, it clamps both stored values to plus or minus 16384 according to their signs.

name: compute_dot_product_inverted
description: Computes the same two dot products and zeroes a third field. When the third dot product is non-negative, it shifts the two stored results right by eight bits and inverts them against the constant 16383.

name: compute_global_vector_dot
description: Computes a dot product between the object's first three components and a global vector stored at a fixed offset from the global base, scales the sum, and stores the negated result in the object.

name: compute_relative_basis_components
description: Compares type bytes of the object and a second object. In one matching case it stores half of the object's own component; otherwise it computes dot products of the object's vectors against the second object's basis and stores them in component fields.

name: select_basis_dot_or_halved
description: When a flag in the object is clear, computes dot products of its vectors with the second object's basis into component fields. When the flag is set, it stores halved values of the object's own components instead.

name: compute_basis_dot_products
description: Computes the first component as a negated dot product of the object's vectors with the second object's basis. When a flag is set, it also computes the other two components the same way.

name: normalize_fixed_point_pair
description: Forms a sign-adjusted magnitude from several accumulator registers and shifts a pair of operands right until the magnitude fits under the limit. A bit-serial loop handles the case where the accumulator is nonzero.

name: normalize_fixed_point_inputs
description: Takes two 32-bit operands, forms a sign-adjusted magnitude from several registers, and shifts both operands right until the magnitude fits under the limit. A bit-serial loop handles the nonzero accumulator case.

name: shift_pair_to_fit_limit
description: Counts how many right shifts bring a value below the limit of 16383, then shifts two input values right by that same count and returns them.

name: invoke_two_handlers
description: Calls an unnamed routine twice in succession and then returns. It does not access memory or registers beyond those calls.

name: dot_or_normalize_by_flag
description: When the object's flag is set and the other object's flag is clear, computes two dot products of the second object's vectors with an input value and returns them shifted. Otherwise it normalizes a pair of values into a bounded range by right-shifting them.

name: add_scaled_offsets_to_pair
description: Obtains a 64-bit value from an unnamed routine and adds two scaled 16-bit fields of the object to its two halves, returning the combined pair.

name: subtract_position_or_negate
description: When a type byte of the object matches a condition against the other object, it obtains a pair from an unnamed routine and subtracts two stored position fields from it. Otherwise it returns those stored fields negated.

name: negate_pair_of_ints
description: Reads two 32-bit fields from the object, negates each one, and returns them as a pair.

name: fetch_or_compute_position_delta
description: Returns a stored pair of position values unless a state byte of the second object equals one. In that case, if a status bit is clear, it calls a dispatch routine and returns the scaled, negated change in two coordinates; otherwise it returns zero.

name: compute_position_delta_via_dispatch
description: If a status bit of the second object is clear, calls a dispatch routine through a function pointer and returns the scaled, negated change in two coordinates. Otherwise it returns zero.

name: integrate_motion_with_timer
description: Normalizes a vector quantity into a fixed-point range and decrements a per-object countdown that triggers recomputation when it expires. When a computed threshold test passes, it accumulates offsets into the object's 64-bit position fields with carry propagation.

name: integrate_motion_from_registers
description: Scales three register inputs into a fixed-point range, updates the object's countdown, and when it expires and a computed threshold test passes, accumulates offsets into the object's 64-bit position fields with carry propagation.

name: integrate_motion_and_clear_accumulators
description: Normalizes a vector into a fixed-point range and decrements a countdown that triggers recomputation. When a threshold test passes, it accumulates offsets into the object's 64-bit position fields and clears the object's motion accumulators.

name: integrate_motion_scaled_offsets
description: Normalizes a 64-bit vector pair into a fixed-point range and counts down the object's timer. When the timer expires and the threshold test passes, it accumulates offsets into the position fields and resets the timer.

name: compute_scaled_motion_vector
description: Normalizes three register inputs into a fixed-point range, stores the scaled result as three components of the object, and, when a countdown test passes, accumulates offsets into its position fields.

name: store_shifted_motion_vector
description: Adds a scaled velocity term to each of three register inputs, stores the three results as components of the object, and returns a pair from an unnamed routine shifted by a variable amount.

name: shift_register_pair_right
description: Shifts two register inputs right by a variable count and returns the pair.

name: forward_single_call
description: Consists of a two-instruction wrapper that calls one other routine. The decompiler timed out, so no further behaviour can be read from the pseudo-code.

name: accumulate_pending_motion_offsets
description: When any of the object's pending offset fields is nonzero, adds them into its 64-bit position fields with carry propagation and clears its motion accumulators. Otherwise it normalizes a vector into a fixed-point range and returns a pair shifted by a computed count.

name: flush_motion_accumulators_to_position
description: Copies a flag byte from the second object when one of its flags is set, then adds a result of an unnamed routine and a stored value to the object's three 64-bit position fields with carry, and clears the motion accumulators.

name: compute_predicted_position_offsets
description: Multiplies three signed velocity components by a fractional scale factor, stores each negated position field minus its scaled term in the object, and returns a pair from an unnamed routine shifted by a variable count.

name: compute_scaled_offsets_from_vector
description: Scales three signed components of the object by a fractional factor, subtracts the stored position fields from the results, stores the three values, and returns a pair from an unnamed routine shifted by a variable count.

name: transform_normalized_vector
description: Shifts three register inputs right until their largest magnitude fits under the limit, then computes two dot products of the shifted vector with rows of the object's matrix and returns them.

name: multiply_vector_by_matrix
description: Computes two output values as dot products of three input words with rows of the object's matrix, scaled by a fixed right shift, and returns them as a pair.

name: clamp_components_to_limits
description: Clamps three input components between per-object lower and upper limits stored in the object, then stores the clamped results in its three component fields.

name: clamp_components_with_floor
description: Raises the second input to a floor value, clamps the other two inputs between per-object limits, and stores the three results in the object's component fields.

name: clamp_and_store_components
description: Clamps the second and third inputs between per-object limits and stores the first input unchanged along with the two clamped values in the object's component fields.

name: floor_and_clamp_components
description: Raises the second input to a floor value, clamps the third between per-object limits, and stores the first input with both results in the object's component fields.

name: clamp_third_component_store
description: Clamps the third input between per-object limits and stores all three inputs in the object's component fields.

name: raise_third_component_to_floor
description: Raises the third input to a floor value and stores all three inputs in the object's component fields.

name: store_three_components_unchanged
description: Stores three input values directly into the object's component fields without any limits.

name: accumulate_weighted_matrix_product
description: Normalizes an input magnitude into a fixed-point range, forms a weighted sum of the object's matrix terms scaled by that value, and adds the result into its 64-bit position accumulators, shifting first when a shift count is available.

name: accumulate_weighted_matrix_saturating
description: Forms the same weighted matrix product as its neighbour but adds it into the position accumulators with saturation, clamping each component to the range the accumulator can represent and skipping the update on overflow.

name: add_components_with_overflow_check
description: Adds two inputs into 16-bit fields of the object and accumulates three inputs into its 64-bit position fields, skipping the position update when an overflow check fails.

name: store_and_accumulate_position_pair
description: Adds an input into a 16-bit field of the object, stores one input directly into the first position field, and accumulates the other two inputs into the remaining position fields, skipping the update on overflow.

name: clamp_and_add_value
description: Raises the third input to a minimum threshold, adds the fourth input to it, and stores the result with two other inputs in the object's position fields.

name: accumulate_clamped_offsets_checked
description: Shifts three register inputs right by a variable count, clamps each one against the object's stored limits, and adds them to its position fields, skipping the update if any addition would overflow.

name: add_clamped_offsets_from_registers
description: Clamps three register inputs against bounds and adds them to the object's position fields, leaving all fields unchanged if any addition overflows.

name: add_offset_and_clamped_pair
description: Adds an unchanged input to the first position field and two clamped inputs to the other two fields, leaving all fields unchanged if any addition overflows.

name: add_clamped_pair_with_input
description: Adds the first input unchanged to the first position field and clamps the second and third inputs into the other two fields, leaving all fields unchanged if any addition overflows.

name: add_offsets_with_clamped_third
description: Adds two inputs unchanged to the first two position fields and a clamped third input to the last, leaving all fields unchanged if any addition overflows.

name: add_two_offsets_clamped_third
description: Adds two register inputs to the first two position fields and a clamped third input to the last, leaving all fields unchanged if any addition overflows.

name: add_offsets_overflow_checked
description: Adds three inputs to the object's three position fields, leaving them unchanged if any addition would overflow.

name: add_scaled_vector_to_position
description: When a flag in the object is set, normalizes its offset vector, scales it by a factor taken from the second object, and adds the result to the object's position fields with carry, returning a magnitude value. Returns zero when the flag is clear.

name: add_scaled_input_to_position
description: When the second object has a nonzero scale field, normalizes three input values, scales them by a factor from that object, and adds the result into the object's position fields with carry.

name: scale_and_add_position_offsets
description: Scales three register inputs by a factor and a shift count, then adds them into the object's position fields, using the fractional accumulators when the shift is non-negative.

name: shift_and_accumulate
description: Right-shifts three input values by a variable count when that count is non-negative, then adds them to the object's three position fields.

name: merge_position_with_other_object
description: Copies a state byte from the second object and adds its three 64-bit position accumulators into the object's accumulators with carry. It then adds a result of an unnamed routine into the object's position fields.

name: subtract_entity_position
description: Copies a state byte from a register into the object, subtracts the second object's three 64-bit position accumulators from its own with borrow, and subtracts a result of an unnamed routine from its position fields.

name: find_nearest_matching_entry
description: Scans a table of entries backwards, skipping those without a flag bit, and keeps the entry whose computed distance-like metric to the target is smallest, updating the best candidate as it goes.

name: select_nearest_and_update_position
description: Searches a table of entries for the one nearest to the object, copies that entry's state byte into the object, and updates its position accumulators with carry or borrow using the matching entry's position.

name: match_table_entry_and_update
description: Scans table entries backwards for one matching a state byte and a distance threshold, copies the state byte into the object and updates its position accumulators from the chosen entry, or from the best candidate found.

name: add_entry_position_to_object
description: Copies a state byte from the second object, adds its three 64-bit position accumulators into the object's with carry, and adds a result of an unnamed routine into its position fields.

name: add_entry_position_after_setup
description: Calls a setup routine, copies a state byte from the second object, adds its three 64-bit position accumulators into the object's with carry, and adds a result of an unnamed routine into its position fields.

name: clear_flag_and_scan_table
description: Clears one flag bit in a global status byte and, if that bit was previously clear, scans a table backwards for entries with another flag bit set, resetting each matching entry's fields through an unnamed routine.

name: select_and_submit_coordinates
description: Chooses one of two sets of four 16-bit values from the object depending on a flag, refreshing the selection first when the flag is set, and passes them to an unnamed routine.

name: copy_matrix_to_buffer
description: Copies eight 16-bit words from the object into a buffer addressed by the global base, zeroes two 32-bit slots, sets two more constants, and calls unnamed routines before and after.

name: transform_object_matrix
description: Decrements a refresh counter, clamping it at zero, and multiplies the object's matrix rows by cached basis vectors to store transformed vectors in the global structure. The transform repeats for a second set when a flag is set.

name: compute_relative_position_fixed
description: Subtracts a reference object's position accumulators from the current position with borrow, normalizes the three differences into a fixed-point range, stores them in the global structure, and copies four constants selected by a table index.

name: compute_relative_position_linked
description: Follows a parent link on the object while a flag is set, subtracts the reference object's position accumulators from the current position, normalizes the differences into a fixed-point range, stores them in the global structure, and copies four constants chosen by a table index.

name: load_table_into_buffer
description: Normalizes a value into a fixed-point range, stores three word values in the global structure, and copies four long constants from a global table selected by the low bits of a status byte.

name: scan_table_and_update_entries
description: Sets a global status bit, then scans a table backwards for entries with another flag bit set. For each one it runs an unnamed routine, updates the entry's state flags and timers, and resets its fields when the object's type matches the global type value.

name: update_entries_by_type_match
description: Scans a table of entries backwards for ones with a flag bit set. For each one it updates state fields and timers, resetting the entry's fields when its type matches the global type value and otherwise calling an unnamed routine.

name: reset_and_scan_entries
description: Resets a pair of fields on an entry, then scans table entries backwards for ones with a flag bit set, updating each entry's state, timers and counters through unnamed routines.

name: scan_entries_with_countdown
description: Scans table entries backwards for ones with a flag bit set. For each one, it stores a fixed value into the object's field and calls an unnamed routine when the countdown byte is zero; otherwise it decrements that countdown byte.

name: restart_scan_on_countdown
description: Stores a word into the global structure, then scans table entries backwards for ones with a flag bit set and calls an unnamed routine for each. When the global countdown byte is zero the scan restarts from the stored word; otherwise the countdown is decremented.

name: advance_object_position_from_table
description: Looks up a table entry for the object's current state, chooses one of several direction vectors according to flag bits, and negates the object's own vectors in one case. It computes a scaled displacement, adds it to the object's 64-bit position fields with carry, and sets its timer to 190.

name: advance_position_from_flag_table
description: Chooses a direction vector from a table entry according to flag bits, negating the object's own vectors in one case, then computes a scaled displacement and adds it to the object's 64-bit position fields with carry.

name: advance_position_and_reset_timer
description: Computes a scaled displacement from a table entry and direction vectors, adds it to the object's 64-bit position fields with carry, sets its timer to 190, and calls an unnamed routine.

name: clear_countdown_byte
description: Sets the object's countdown byte to zero and returns.

name: clear_timer_and_scan_entries
description: Clears a global timer word, then scans table entries backwards for nonzero entries that lack a flag bit, calling two unnamed routines for each.

name: iterate_and_call_handler
description: Scans table entries backwards and, for each nonzero entry whose flag bit is clear, calls an unnamed routine and then an indirect handler held in a register.

name: check_bounds_and_call
description: Scans table entries backwards, skipping entries with one flag bit set. For each entry without a second flag bit, it checks two of the object's coordinates against fixed bounds and calls a handler when both are inside them.

name: decrement_counter_and_dispatch
description: Scans table entries backwards for ones with a flag bit set and decrements a countdown byte in each. When the countdown reaches zero it reloads it and calls a dispatch handler selected by the entry's type byte.

name: clear_flag_and_dispatch_entries
description: Clears a global status bit, then scans table entries backwards for ones with another flag bit set. For each one it calls an unnamed routine and, when the entry's type byte is nonzero, calls a dispatch handler selected by that type.

name: write_byte_to_indirect
description: Writes a byte input into a memory location computed from a global base pointer plus the object's index byte.

name: store_record_in_flagged_slot
description: Finds the first table slot whose flag bit is set, stores a status byte there and adjusts a global counter, copies a fixed-size record from the input into that slot, and when a further parameter is nonzero initializes the slot's motion fields with shifted values.

name: store_record_in_clear_slot
description: Finds a table slot whose flag bit is clear and, if it lies beyond a reserved index range, stores a status byte there, copies a fixed-size record from the input into it, and initializes its motion fields with shifted values when a further parameter is nonzero.

name: store_record_at_index
description: Stores a status byte at a given index in a table, adjusts a global counter, copies a fixed-size record into the slot for that index, and when a further parameter is nonzero initializes the motion fields with shifted values.

name: copy_record_and_initialize
description: Copies a fixed-size record from one buffer to another unless they are the same, then when a parameter is nonzero initializes the copy's motion fields with shifted values and sets its type and timing fields from a lookup.

name: store_record_in_free_slot
description: Finds a free table slot at or above a reserved index, or else a slot whose flag bit is clear, stores a status byte and a fixed-size record there, and when a further parameter is nonzero initializes its motion fields with shifted values.

name: store_record_in_empty_slot
description: Finds a table slot that is empty or has a clear flag bit, stores a status byte and a fixed-size record there, and when a further parameter is nonzero initializes its motion fields with shifted values. Otherwise it returns the parameter unchanged.

name: stub_return_standard_exit
description: Contains only a standard return and performs no work.

name: stub_return_immediate_exit
description: Contains only a return and performs no work.

name: stub_empty_no_operation
description: Contains only a return and performs no work. Several routines call it.

name: stub_single_return
description: A single return instruction that does nothing. Seven routines call it.

name: stub_return_void
description: Contains only a return instruction and does nothing.

name: clear_buffer_from_pointer
description: Stores a buffer pointer into a global slot and then zeroes a fixed-length block of bytes starting at that pointer.

name: clear_flagged_table_entries
description: Resets a global counter to zero, then scans table entries backwards and clears each entry whose flag bit is set.

name: clear_entry_and_decrement
description: Reads the object's index byte, decrements a global counter when the indexed table entry has a flag bit set, and then clears that table entry.

name: call_clear_entry_wrapper
description: Calls one unnamed routine and returns. It is a thin wrapper around the entry clearing step.

name: clear_entry_after_notifying_handlers
description: Reads the object's index byte. When the indexed table entry's flag bit is clear, it calls the notification handler of each registered slot whose flag bit is set and then clears the entry; otherwise it decrements a global counter and clears the entry.

name: notify_handlers_then_subtract_counter
description: Notifies registered handlers, then either calls an unnamed routine and returns one when the entry is flagged or a lookup value is zero. Otherwise it subtracts the input from a counter field, and when that counter underflows it updates the entry's fields and returns zero.

name: call_handler_return_one
description: Calls a handler through a function pointer in the global structure and returns a pair whose high word is one and whose low word is the register input.

name: call_handler_set_status_bit
description: Calls a global handler, sets bit 0 of the object's status byte, calls a second handler when the object's marker byte is minus one, and returns one.

name: process_object_state_update
description: Optionally adds a table-derived amount to a global counter and calls a callback when the counter's high word changes. It then calls unnamed routines and, depending on a field of the object, invokes a handler and may repeat an unnamed routine for each step within a range.

name: return_stack_argument
description: Returns the value passed on the stack without other work.

name: initialize_object_and_add_offset
description: Calls an unnamed routine and, when it does not signal, sets the object's type, timing and state fields, then adds two values obtained from unnamed routines to its position fields and returns the result of a final unnamed routine call.

name: classify_fetched_value_range
description: Calls an unnamed routine and, when the object's marker byte is minus one and a looked-up value is below a limit, finds the matching bracket in a table and decrements its counter. Otherwise it classifies a freshly fetched value into ranges, tallying counters from a table or clearing a per-object slot, then invokes callbacks for marked objects.

name: extract_flag_from_mask
description: Draws an index from an unnamed routine a limited number of times until it hits a bit set in the object's source mask, then moves that bit from the source mask into the destination mask.

name: tally_value_range_and_clear
description: Classifies an input value into one of three ranges. Below the first limit it adds a table-derived amount to global counters when a flag is set; in the middle range it applies a reduced amount; otherwise it clears a per-object slot. It then runs callbacks when the object's marker byte is minus one.

name: tally_state_byte_and_clear
description: Reads and clears a state byte and a timer word on the object. When the object is marked, it adds a table-derived amount to global counters, then invokes a callback and an unnamed routine and returns one.

name: tally_state_byte_minus_four
description: When the object's state byte is nonzero, sets it to one and, if the object is marked, adds a table-derived amount reduced by four to global counters. It then invokes a callback and an unnamed routine and returns one.

name: tally_input_bracket
description: When the input value is below a limit, finds the matching bracket in a table, decrements that bracket's counter and increments a global tally. It invokes a callback for marked objects and returns one.

name: update_object_timers_and_budget
description: Ramps and decays several per-object fields, computes a magnitude-weighted cost from the object's three components and subtracts it from a budget word. When the budget is exhausted it consumes a global allowance or invokes a callback, then clears the three component fields and returns the cost.

name: spend_budget_or_clear_components
description: Subtracts an input amount from a per-object budget word. When the budget is exhausted it consumes a global allowance or invokes a callback, and then clears three component fields.

name: refill_budget_or_flag_callback
description: When a global allowance counter is nonzero, decrements it, increments a second global tally and adds a fixed refill to the object's budget word. Otherwise it sets a global status bit, invokes a callback once, and clears three component fields.

name: refill_budget_or_clear_components
description: When a per-object counter is nonzero, decrements it and adds a fixed refill to the budget word. Otherwise it clears three component fields.

name: set_flag_and_call_handler
description: Sets bit 0 of a global status byte and, if that bit was previously clear, calls a handler through the global table. It then clears three component fields of the object.

name: tick_timer_and_tally_expiry
description: Subtracts an input from a global timer. When the timer wraps it reloads it, decrements two global counters, runs an unnamed routine, and when the result passes a threshold it flushes the object's pending tally and invokes a callback.

name: reload_timer_and_tally_expiry
description: Reloads a global timer, decrements two global counters, runs an unnamed routine, and when the result passes a threshold it flushes the object's pending tally and invokes a callback.

name: flush_pending_tally
description: When the object's pending byte is nonzero, clears it and the budget word, adds a table-derived amount to global counters, and invokes a callback.

name: flush_pending_tally_if_over
description: Calls an unnamed routine and, when its result exceeds a global threshold and the object's pending byte is nonzero, flushes the pending tally into global counters and invokes a callback.

name: flush_pending_tally_conditional
description: Calls an unnamed routine and, when the zero flag is set and the result exceeds a global threshold while the object has a pending byte, flushes that tally into global counters. It then invokes a callback unless it returned early.

name: set_state_and_dispatch
description: Stores the input value as the current state word and, if the previous state was nonzero, calls the handler registered for that previous state through the global table.

name: store_state_word
description: Stores the input value into the global state word.

name: lookup_scaled_table_value
description: Maps an input value through a global lookup table, choosing the index scale from the magnitude range of the input and shifting the table entry right by a matching amount before returning it.

name: initialize_entity_table
description: Writes seed constants, handler pointers and table pointers into the global structure, then walks the table of handler slots, copying each slot's pointer into the next field and invoking its handler.

name: initialize_and_iterate_table
description: Initializes global counters and, for small inputs, resets two seed constants. It then walks the table of handler slots repeatedly, calling the handler stored in each slot, until a fixed count is reached.

name: run_periodic_slot_handlers
description: Clears status bits and calls a handler for each flagged slot. When a free-running counter has advanced by a fixed period, it runs a second set of handlers with the number of elapsed periods, then calls handlers for entries flagged in the table.

name: call_handler_if_active
description: Walks the handler slots and calls the handler at each slot's second entry point for every slot whose active byte is nonzero.

name: dispatch_matching_key_handler
description: When a status bit is clear, obtains a key from an unnamed routine and searches the table of handler slots for a matching key byte. On a match it calls an unnamed routine and the matched slot's handler; otherwise it calls a fallback routine.

name: call_handler_by_bit_mask
description: Maps the input code to a bit position and calls the handler of each table slot whose flag byte has that bit set.

name: update_pseudo_random_state
description: Advances two 32-bit global state words with a shift, exclusive-or and addition update that produces a pseudo-random sequence.

name: compute_scaled_random_value
description: Advances the two global state words with a shift and addition update, then returns the input scaled by the high half of the new state.

name: scale_input_by_state
description: Multiplies the input by a value derived from the global state words and returns the scaled result.

name: negate_64_bit_value
description: Obtains a 64-bit value from an unnamed routine and returns its two's complement negation, propagating the carry between the halves.

name: multiply_64_bit_fixed_point
description: Subtracts one 64-bit operand from another and, when the result is non-negative, multiplies it by a 32-bit factor with 16-bit partial products and returns a shifted fixed-point product. When the result is negative it returns the negated value from an unnamed routine instead.

name: perform_32x32_multiplication
description: Multiplies two 32-bit operands using 16-bit partial products and carries, and returns a 64-bit result shifted with extra status bits.

name: compute_scaled_difference_fields
description: Computes two differences from results of unnamed routines, scales them by a fixed-point fraction derived from the input, and stores six 32-bit values into the object, shifting or looping over bits depending on a count.

name: store_components_with_scaled_copies
description: Stores three input values into the object's first position fields and three register values shifted left by a count into its second set of fields.

name: accumulate_scaled_vector
description: Scales three 16-bit components of the object by a fixed-point factor, shifts the products by a count through a bit-serial loop, and adds them into the object's 64-bit position fields with carry.

name: normalize_and_double_result
description: Counts the bit length of the register input, obtains a 64-bit value from an unnamed routine, and shifts that value left by the count before returning it.

name: shift_helper_result_by_count
description: Counts how many right shifts bring the register input below 32768, obtains a 64-bit value from an unnamed routine, and shifts that value left by the same count.

name: negate_helper_64_bit_result
description: Calls an unnamed routine and returns the 64-bit two's complement negation of its result.

name: multiply_or_shift_by_magnitude
description: Negates the result of an unnamed routine when a register input is negative. Otherwise it multiplies two 32-bit values by a fixed-point factor when the input is zero, or counts shifts and shifts the 64-bit result of an unnamed routine left by that count.

name: multiply_or_shift_by_flag
description: Uses the processor's zero flag to choose between a fixed-point multiply of two 32-bit values and a shift of the 64-bit result of an unnamed routine by a bit count. The result is returned as a 64-bit pair.

name: multiply_or_shift_fixed_point
description: Multiplies two 32-bit values by a fixed-point factor when the scaled input is small enough. Otherwise it counts the right shifts needed to bring the input under 32768, obtains a 64-bit value from an unnamed routine, and shifts it left by that count.

name: multiply_and_round
description: Multiplies two 32-bit operands by a 16-bit factor using word-sized partial products and carries, then shifts each result right by one bit to round it.

name: add_64bit_to_128bit_accumulator
description: Obtains a 64-bit value from an unnamed routine and adds it into a 128-bit accumulator in the object with carry propagation, together with two of the object's position fields and a register input.

name: call_two_helpers
description: Calls two unnamed routines in succession and returns.

name: call_helper_pair_once
description: Calls two unnamed routines in succession and returns.

name: call_helper_pair_sequence
description: Calls two unnamed routines in succession and returns.

name: fetch_table_entry
description: Returns the 16-bit value at an offset from the table base pointer held in the global structure, using the input register as the offset.

name: set_table_base_pointers
description: Stores two address inputs as the table base pointers in the global structure.

name: reset_table_base_pointers
description: Resets the two table base pointers in the global structure to the global data area.

name: allocate_small_table_slot
description: If the slot at the input index is unused and a global allocation offset is below a limit, stores that offset in the slot, writes the slot index and offset as a pair at the offset position, and advances the offset by four.

name: allocate_indexed_table_slot
description: If an allocation offset is below a limit, stores the offset as a byte in an indexed table, writes the index and offset as a pair at that offset, advances the offset by four and returns the pair. Otherwise it returns zero.

name: write_byte_and_index
description: Stores a byte at an index in a table, writes the index and a second value as a pair at a pointer-relative offset, and advances that pointer by four.

name: stub_return_nothing
description: Contains only a return and performs no work.

name: check_coordinates_in_bounds
description: Checks two coordinate pairs against the display bounds, transforming each out-of-range pair through an unnamed routine and rechecking it. It calls a follow-on routine only when both pairs lie within the bounds.

name: call_single_helper_return
description: Calls one unnamed routine and returns.

name: check_bounds_then_call
description: Checks two coordinate pairs against the display bounds, transforming out-of-range pairs through an unnamed routine, and calls a follow-on routine only when both are inside.

name: check_single_point_then_call
description: Transforms the input coordinate through an unnamed routine, and calls a follow-on routine only when the result lies within the display bounds.

name: mark_object_status_on_flags
description: Checks two flag bits of the object. When either is set, it sets global status bits, sets a countdown byte to two, updates the object's status bits and calls an unnamed routine. Otherwise it returns unchanged.

name: set_status_flags_and_call
description: Sets two global status bits and a countdown byte to two on the object, updates the object's status bits, and calls an unnamed routine.

name: set_flag_and_call_helper
description: Sets a global status bit, sets the object's countdown byte to two, updates its status bits and calls an unnamed routine.

name: clear_flag_and_schedule_timer
description: When a flag bit of the object is set, clears it and advances a timer by four. The timer is a global one when the object's marker byte is minus one, otherwise it belongs to the object. It then sets a countdown byte to seven, updates status bits, calls two unnamed routines and sets a global status bit.

name: set_flags_and_schedule_timer
description: Stores a flags word into the object, advances the same timer as its neighbour by four, sets a countdown byte to seven, updates status bits, calls two unnamed routines and sets a global status bit.

name: advance_timer_and_schedule
description: Advances the object's own timer by four, sets a countdown byte to seven, updates its status bits, calls two unnamed routines and sets a global status bit.

name: check_index_then_call
description: When the object's index is below a limit and differs from the second object, calls an unnamed routine and then calls a follow-on routine if a computed value is below a threshold.

name: apply_table_driven_motion
description: Looks up a per-state table entry, marks the object's status bits, and derives a fixed-point motion scale from table values and the object's velocity. It applies a shifted amount to the object's timer or lookup value and, for one special object index, copies a stored six-long record before running follow-on unnamed routines.

name: apply_table_limit_to_object
description: Looks up a table value from the global state index and either sets the object's limit fields or adds a scaled, clamped amount to its accumulator. It then calls an unnamed routine and returns the shifted result.

name: add_saturating_scaled_amount
description: Multiplies the input by a table-scaled factor, adds the clamped result to the object's accumulator field with saturation, calls an unnamed routine, and returns the shifted value.

name: apply_coefficient_driven_motion
description: Sets a status bit, computes a fixed-point scale from the second object's coefficients and the object's own values, and applies a table-derived amount to the object's accumulator. It then runs the special-index record copy and follow-on unnamed routines as its neighbour does.

name: apply_flagged_coefficient_motion
description: Sets a status bit, selects one of two coefficient pairs from the second object by a flag, computes a scaled motion value, and applies a table-derived amount to the object's accumulator. It then runs the special-index record copy and follow-on unnamed routines.

name: apply_coefficient_motion_plain
description: Computes a scaled motion value from the second object's coefficients and applies a table-derived amount to the object's accumulator, then runs the same follow-on steps as its neighbours.

name: store_accumulators_and_initialize
description: When a global counter is nonzero and a flag or a test from an unnamed routine passes, stores six 32-bit values into the second object's accumulators, sets its type and timing fields, and calls an unnamed routine. It then adjusts a per-object counter according to two input bits and returns the result of an unnamed routine.

name: return_stack_value
description: Returns the value passed on the stack without other work.

name: clear_pending_and_set_label
description: Clears a pending byte in the object's slot list and, when the object is not of the special type, updates a counter, sets the object's type and state bytes from input flag bits, copies a text label from global data into its label field, and calls an unnamed routine. The routine then returns minus one.

name: set_label_text_and_type
description: Updates a counter in the object, sets its type and state bytes from input flag bits, and copies the label text referenced as "Mine" from global data into its label field. It calls an unnamed routine and returns minus one.

name: set_missile_label_and_type
description: Sets a fixed value in the second object's field, copies the label text referenced as "Missile" from global data into its label field, sets its owner and timing bytes, and calls an unnamed routine. It returns minus one.

name: set_type_and_owner_fields
description: Calls an unnamed routine, raises the first object's type byte to a fixed value and records the second object's index as owner when the type is below that value, copies a source byte into the second object, resets its timing word, calls an unnamed routine and returns minus one.

name: call_helper_return_minus_one
description: Calls one unnamed routine and returns minus one.

name: add_signed_fixed_values
description: Adds three signed 32-bit fixed-point register values into the second object's three 64-bit accumulators, propagating carries from the sign of each value.

name: assign_code_to_global_slot
description: Checks whether the input code already occupies one of four global slots. If it does, it stores fixed values for a few codes and returns. Otherwise it writes the input value into a per-code global word and, depending on the slot, clears a 32-word buffer and records the code in a slot register.

name: assign_code_to_alt_slot
description: Variant of its neighbour that tests a different pair of global slot values before deciding whether to clear the buffer. Otherwise it performs the same slot assignment.
